name: colRanks
title: Gets the rank of the elements in each column of a matrix

origin.description: Gets the rank of the elements in each row (column) of a matrix.
origin.usage:
colRanks(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, ties.method = c("max", "average",
  "first", "last", "random", "max", "min", "dense"), dim. = dim(x),
  preserveShape = FALSE, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: ties.method
arguments.text: A character string specifying how ties are treated. The installed default is max. Partial matches follow charmatch against average, first, last, random, max, min, and dense.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when x is not a matrix.

arguments.name: preserveShape
arguments.text: If TRUE, the result has the same shape as the selected matrix. If FALSE, that matrix is transposed.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: Each column is ranked on its own, with the same tie and missing-value rules as rowRanks. The native result has one row per selected row. When preserveShape is FALSE, which is the default, that matrix is transposed, so each column of ranks is returned as a row.
origin.value: A matrix of type integer, or double when ties.method is average. With preserveShape TRUE the shape is N by K. Otherwise it is K by N.

translation.description: Gets the rank of the elements in each column of a matrix.
translation.usage: colRanks(x, rows=None, cols=None, ties_method="max", dim=None, preserve_shape=False, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Ranks use only the selected rows, in this order.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and a missing index is ranked as NA.

arguments.name: ties_method
arguments.text: How ties are ranked. This is ties.method. The default is max. The accepted values are the same unique prefixes as rowRanks.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: preserve_shape
arguments.text: This is preserveShape. False, the default, transposes the ranked matrix so each column of ranks is a row. True keeps one row per selected row.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate rowranks, ported from matrixStats src/rowRanksWithTies.c with byrow false. Each selected column is ranked across the selected rows. Missing values and ties follow rowRanks. The native matrix has shape (N, K). preserve_shape false returns its transpose, shape (K, N).
translation.value: An array. average returns float64. Every other method returns int32. preserve_shape false has shape (K, N). preserve_shape true has shape (N, K).
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowranks import colRanks

x = np.array([3, 1, 3, 2]).reshape((2, 2), order="F")
colRanks(x, ties_method="max")
